chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Danny Williams's parents and the Williams Singers
summary: Jones knows only that the Williams Singers were famous spiritual singers who had broken up before he joined Danny.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: You mentioned Danny Williams' parents, The Williams Singers --
-- had been very big at the turn of the century. What kind of singing did they do? Do you know anything
about them, other than that they were just very prominent, and I think you said they toured internationally, didn't you?
Yes, they did. They were -- well, let me see. In those days spirituals were very big, you know?
Like the Hall-Johnson Choir and the Williams Singers, and they -- people like maybe Roland Hayes or Paul Robeson. That was a big thing in those days, you know?
But you said that they went back to the turn of the century, so that would be --
Even before these other people you mentioned.
That's why I was kind of interested to know what you may have remembered about them.
I didn't -- I never heard them. By the time I was with Danny, oh they had long broken up.
You know? Because we came along way later, you know.
Because we were kids at that point. You know.
